A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Skill Neologisms research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching content across appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original XOR/XNOR experiments, synthetic digit-operation learning and composition results, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds natural-language Skill-Mix experiments and a skill-label-noise analysis.

M1.justification: The frozen-model procedure, skill-centered training, vocabulary-integrated soft tokens and optimization objective remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. Skill-Mix uses the previously described word-replacement insertion mechanism rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Section 6 adds natural-language generation on Skill-Mix, targeting modus ponens and statistical syllogism and mixing them with other language skills during training. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained binary-operation and synthetic digit-transformation tasks.

E2.justification: The new Skill-Mix comparison includes an unadapted Llama3.2-3B-Instruct reference in Figure 7. LoRA and prompt tuning are reused comparators; their extension to Skill-Mix is not itself a baseline addition. Comparator membership in the original experiments, including the ICL comparison, remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Skill-Mix introduces a distinct protocol using Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, 300 GPT-5-generated training examples per target skill, 50 joint-skill test queries and GPT-5 grading. The noise experiment adds controlled corruption of training skill labels. Previously reported synthetic-task splits and budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.3.3 and Appendix A.6 add a bounded sensitivity study asking how inaccurate skill labels affect learning and composition: INV-POL, held-out ADD and five soft tokens, with varying corruption levels. The existing length, composition-complexity and initialization ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The existing binomial standard errors and standard deviations across held-out configurations or ICL example-count settings remain unchanged. The added Skill-Mix and noise plots introduce no repeated-seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds natural-language results, including approximately 70% joint-skill success with combined neologisms versus 6% for the unadapted model. Figure A4 adds evidence that composition deteriorates under label noise, even while single-operation performance remains comparatively robust. These are new experiments; the earlier numerical results are retained unchanged.

T1.justification: The closed-form assumption, compositional notation, Definitions 3.1–3.2 and training objective are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central continual-learning thesis and three desired properties remain unchanged. The abstract, contribution list and conclusion now explicitly claim natural-language validation on Skill-Mix, while the abstract identifies the earlier demonstration as a controlled synthetic task.

C2.justification: The discussion replaces the synthetic-only applicability caveat with a remaining limitation concerning fuzzy definitions of skills and their compositions. The noise study adds a concrete qualification concerning annotation quality. Existing limitations concerning dataset construction, soft-token optimization and computational cost remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds code repository links and substantial Skill-Mix reproduction information in Appendix D.3: training-data construction, hyperparameters, inference and grading prompts, and insertion examples. Appendix D.2.1 newly discloses random padding within a 128-token limit for existing pretraining; this does not establish that the procedure changed between versions.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive novelty positioning are retained. Citations and behavioral-alignment context added to the main discussion were already present in v1 Appendix B. Author, venue and publication-year corrections concern the same referenced works.

P1.justification: v3 makes widespread but limited copyedits, standardizes terminology, distinguishes algorithmic and natural-language experiments, and consolidates experimental details under Appendix D. It also corrects the Appendix A.5 heading and adds impact and acknowledgment sections. Most existing exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 7, Figure A4 and prompt listings, removes the redundant hyperparameter-summary Table E7, and relocates existing displays. Original graphics remain unchanged. Caption corrections include removing Figure 2's reference to a nonexistent panel D.

improvement.justification: The natural-language experiment substantially strengthens the central composition claim beyond v1's explicitly acknowledged synthetic-only demonstration. The noise analysis tests an important practical vulnerability, and detailed prompts and settings improve reproducibility. The gains remain bounded: Skill-Mix covers one model, two target skills and 50 GPT-5-graded queries without uncertainty estimates, so broader continual-learning generality remains unestablished.
